literal: When envoys from Liang were about to arrive, he was ordered to receive them as host.
idiomatic: When envoys from Liang were due to arrive, the court ordered Hongxun to receive them.

literal: Emperor Gaozu had once campaigned as far as Bingzhou and composed the Record of the Jin Shrine; lovers of letters prized its prose.
idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had once marched to Bingzhou and written the Record of the Jin Shrine, and men who cared for letters treasured its prose.

literal: He rose to Grand Administrator of Gaoyang. In office he was austere and pure; his wife and children could not escape cold and hunger, and opinion of the day held him in high esteem.
idiomatic: He rose to Grand Administrator of Gaoyang, where he served with austere integrity—so much so that his wife and children still knew cold and hunger—and contemporaries held him in high regard.

literal: At the opening of the Tianbao era he died in office.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he died in office.

literal: Li Guang, styled Hongji, was a man of Fanyang; his ancestors had moved there from Liaodong.
idiomatic: Li Guang, styled Hongji, was from Fanyang; his forebears had moved there from Liaodong.

literal: Guang read widely among the classics and possessed talent, reflection, and the beauty of literary discourse. In youth he shared fame with Li Jian of Zhao commandery, ranking just below Xing Shao and Wei Shou.
idiomatic: Guang had read widely in the classics and possessed talent, reflection, and a gift for literary argument. In his youth he stood equal in reputation with Li Jian of Zhao commandery, second only to Xing Shao and Wei Shou.

literal: Yet he was slow of speech and quick in action.
idiomatic: Yet he was slow of tongue and swift in deed.

literal: When Prince Anfeng of Wei Yuan Yanming guarded Xuzhou, he appointed Guang Senior Staff Officer for Current Affairs.
idiomatic: When Prince Anfeng of Wei, Yuan Yanming, held Xuzhou, he appointed Guang senior staff officer for current affairs.

literal: At first appointment he was made Pacification General.
idiomatic: On first entering service he was made Pacification General.

literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan requisitioned him as Record Keeper to the Grand General with the additional title Remonstrance Grand Master.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan summoned him as record keeper to the Grand General, with the additional title Remonstrance Grand Master.

literal: Xingzao of the Jingzhou frontier staff memorialized him up as Bureau Gentleman on the frontier staff; soon he was Recorder in the Office of the Chariots and Cavalry.
idiomatic: Xingzao of the Jingzhou frontier staff had him promoted to bureau gentleman on the staff; before long he was recorder in the Office of the Chariots and Cavalry.

literal: Censor-in-Chief Cui Xuan rigorously selected censors—all were sons of noble houses; Guang alone, on learning and talent, was made censor while also editing the national history.
idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Cui Xuan chose his censors with exacting care, and every appointee was a son of a noble house—Guang alone won the post on learning and talent, and while serving as censor he also edited the national history.

literal: Most memorials from the Southern Terrace bore his phrasing.
idiomatic: Most of the Southern Terrace's official documents carried his phrasing.

literal: Duke of Pingyang Yan appointed him vice censor; he was transferred to Palace Censor.
idiomatic: Duke of Pingyang Yan appointed him vice censor, then transferred him to palace censor.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xianzu's inheritance of the hegemony, Guang was ordered to keep the records.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzu first took up the hegemony, Guang was ordered to keep the records.

literal: At the opening of Tianbao he was to be made Secretariat Gentleman, but the appointment stopped when his illness grew grave.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he was to be made secretariat gentleman, but his illness turned grave and the appointment was set aside.

literal: Once, going early to court before it was light, he dozed off and suddenly started awake, telling his wife: I seemed to be asleep when I saw a man come out of my body and say, Your mind works too hard—what the spirit cannot bear; I now take my leave of you.
idiomatic: Once, on his way to early court while it was still dark, he dozed and suddenly started awake. He told his wife, "I seemed to sleep, then saw a man step out of my body and say, 'You tax your mind past what the spirit can bear—I now take my leave of you.'"

literal: From this he was confused and unhappy; within days he fell ill, and for years he could not rise. His assets were emptied again and again, and medicine ran out.
idiomatic: After that he was dazed and low in spirit; within days he fell ill and for years could not rise. His household was emptied again and again, until there was no money left for medicine.

literal: Guang had fine discernment, broad magnanimity, and was level and unselfish; the gentry loved him, and each year they sent him gifts on which he relied to live.
idiomatic: Guang had a keen eye, a wide measure, and a level hand without favor; men of standing loved him, and year by year they sent him gifts on which he managed to live.

literal: In the end he died of his illness.
idiomatic: In the end he died of his illness.

literal: He had once recommended Bi Yiyun to Cui Xuan. After Guang's death, Yiyun gathered ten juan of his writings and asked Wei Shou to write the preface.
idiomatic: He had once recommended Bi Yiyun to Cui Xuan. After Guang's death, Yiyun gathered ten juan of his writings and entrusted Wei Shou to write the preface.

literal: His clansman Zidao also had literary pieces.
idiomatic: His clansman Zidao also wrote with distinction.

literal: Fan Xun, styled Xiaoqian, was a man of Beiyi in Hedong.
idiomatic: Fan Xun, styled Xiaoqian, was from Beiyi in Hedong.

literal: His grandfather Yan and his father Heng both held no office.
idiomatic: His grandfather Yan and his father Heng both held no office.

literal: Heng was supremely filial. When his father died he carried earth to build the tomb mound and planted cypresses over several tens of mu, mourning morning and evening.
idiomatic: Heng was supremely filial. When his father died he carried earth to raise the mound and planted cypresses over several tens of mu, weeping morning and evening beside them.

literal: Xun studied from youth, and his elder brother Zhong often provided for him generously.
idiomatic: Xun studied from youth, and his elder brother Zhong often provided for him generously.

literal: Then he blamed himself, saying: I am called a younger brother yet alone enjoy ease—can I not be ashamed before my own heart?
idiomatic: Then he reproached himself: "I am called a younger brother, yet I alone enjoy ease—how can I not be ashamed before my own heart?"

literal: He wished to share in the same toil and enterprise.
idiomatic: He wished to share the same labor and ambition.

literal: His mother, Lady Feng, said to him: Do you mean to keep only to petty circumspection?
idiomatic: His mother, Lady Feng, said to him, "Do you mean to keep only to petty circumspection?"

literal: Moved by his mother's words, he devoted himself to the classics and constantly wrote on the wall the four characters see the worthy and think to emulate, to encourage himself.
idiomatic: Moved by his mother's words, he gave himself wholly to the classics and constantly wrote on the wall the four characters "see the worthy and think to emulate," to steel himself.

literal: When his home commandery fell to the enemy he lodged in Ye and served as a minor clerk in Linzhang.
idiomatic: When his home commandery fell to the enemy he lodged in Ye and served as a minor clerk in Linzhang.

literal: Magistrate Pei Jian took office with austere integrity and brought forth omens such as the white sparrow; Xun submitted ten pieces of the Ode to Pure Virtue.
idiomatic: Magistrate Pei Jian took office with austere integrity and drew forth omens such as the white sparrow; Xun submitted ten pieces of the Ode to Pure Virtue.

literal: Jian greatly valued and promoted him to chief clerk, and still recommended him to Right Vice-Director Cui Xuan, together with Li Guang of Liaodong and Feng Xiaoyan of Bohai, as Xuan's literary guests.
idiomatic: Jian prized him greatly, promoted him to chief clerk, and recommended him to Right Vice-Director Cui Xuan—together with Li Guang of Liaodong and Feng Xiaoyan of Bohai—as one of Xuan's literary guests.

literal: Some mocked him for his quiet demeanor and failure to chase the times.
idiomatic: Some mocked his quiet manner and his refusal to chase the fashion of the hour.

literal: Xun often took to heart Dongfang Shuo's words about lying low in the world and avoiding the world at the Golden Horse Gate—why must one be beneath deep mountains and thatched huts? He therefore borrowed the name Lord Lying Low as host, modeled on the Guest's Difficulty, and composed the Guest's Reproach to enlarge his meaning.
idiomatic: Xun often took to heart Dongfang Shuo's counsel about lying low in the world and keeping to the Golden Horse Gate to avoid the age—why must one hide only in deep mountains and thatched huts? He therefore borrowed the name Lord Lying Low as his host, modeled on the Guest's Difficulty, and wrote the Guest's Reproach to give his meaning room.

literal: Later, when Cui Xuan held a great gathering of guests, the Grand Marshal, Prince of Xiangcheng Yuan Xu, was also present, and they discussed whom to appoint to the prince's staff.
idiomatic: Later, when Cui Xuan held a great gathering of guests, Grand Marshal Prince of Xiangcheng Yuan Xu was also seated there, and they discussed whom to appoint to the prince's staff.

literal: Xuan pointed at Xun and said: This man's learning is rich and his talent high; add his fine conduct—he can serve as the prince's army adviser.
idiomatic: Xuan pointed at Xun and said, "This man's learning is deep and his talent high, and his conduct is fine besides—he can serve as the prince's army adviser."

literal: Xu looked at him and said: Could he really take the post?
idiomatic: Xu looked him over and said, "Could he really take such a post?"

literal: Xun said: My house has no hereditary stipend; I dare not accept this.
idiomatic: Xun said, "My house has no hereditary stipend—I dare not accept this."

literal: In the seventh year of Wuding the Emperor passed away; Xuan was moved to the frontier marches and his guests all scattered, and Xun went to live in Chenliu.
idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wuding the Emperor passed away; Xuan was sent to the frontier marches and his guests scattered, and Xun went to settle in Chenliu.

literal: Liu Shagui, governor of Liangzhou, made Xun concurrent recorder and also nominated him as xiucai.
idiomatic: Liu Shagui, governor of Liangzhou, made Xun concurrent recorder and also nominated him as xiucai.

literal: The old rule of the Secretariat held that each lower province presented xiucai once every three years; it had been five years since Kaifeng man Zheng Zuxian was sent up, and by the count this year did not qualify. Vice Governor Wang Cong protested, and Right Assistant Director Yang Fei could not refute him.
idiomatic: The Secretariat's old rule held that each lower province presented xiucai once every three years; five years had already passed since Kaifeng man Zheng Zuxian was sent up, and by the count this year did not qualify. Vice Governor Wang Cong protested, and Right Assistant Director Yang Fei could not set his protest aside.

literal: Shangshu Ling Gao Longzhi said: Though Xun's learning and talent are outstanding, to wait until next year for office is not far off.
idiomatic: Shangshu Ling Gao Longzhi said, "Though Xun's learning and talent are outstanding, to wait until next year for office is not far."

literal: Xun in the end returned to his home province.
idiomatic: Xun in the end returned to his home province.

literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to concurrent chief clerk and followed the army on the southern campaign.
idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to concurrent chief clerk and followed the army on the southern campaign.

literal: When the army returned, Shagui was moved to Yingchuan and again drew Xun as concurrent chief clerk of Yingzhou.
idiomatic: When the army returned, Shagui was moved to Yingchuan and again drew Xun as concurrent chief clerk of Yingzhou.

literal: In the first year of Tianbao his home province again summoned him as xiucai.
idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao his home province again summoned him as xiucai.

literal: In the second year, spring, after the palace examination and policy response ended, Secretariat Gentleman Zhang Zirong memorialized his entry.
idiomatic: In the second year, in spring, after the palace examination and policy response had ended, Secretariat Gentleman Zhang Zirong memorialized his entry.

literal: By the fourth year, fifth month, Xun and Dingzhou xiucai Li Zixuan and others, because three years had passed since the policy response without appointment, were sent outside the ranks; they memorialized asking that their cases be heard and dismissed, but the edict gave no reply.
idiomatic: By the fourth year, in the fifth month, Xun and Dingzhou xiucai Li Zixuan and others—because three years had passed since the policy response without appointment—were sent outside the ranks. They memorialized asking that their cases be heard and dismissed, but the edict gave no reply.

literal: Liangzhou again memorialized Xun as xiucai.
idiomatic: Liangzhou again memorialized Xun as xiucai.

literal: In the fifth year, first month, an imperial edict questioned the title for ascending the central peak; Xun answered:
idiomatic: In the fifth year, in the first month, an imperial edict questioned the title for ascending the central peak; Xun answered:

literal: Your servant has heard that the rite of touring the sacred peaks is engraved in the Document of Yu, and the meaning of surveying the regions is set forth in the Images of the Changes.
idiomatic: Your servant has heard that the rite of touring the sacred peaks is cut into the Document of Yu, and the meaning of surveying the regions is set forth in the Images of the Changes.

literal: Former emperors and early kings were not of a single surname; those who sealed gold and carved jade number more than a hundred million.
idiomatic: Former emperors and early kings were not of a single surname; those who sealed gold and carved jade number beyond counting.

literal: When Zhongni viewed Liangfu he could not know them all;
idiomatic: When Zhongni viewed Liangfu he could not know them all;

literal: what Guan Zhong answered Duke Huan of Qi preserved was only a few.
idiomatic: what Guan Zhong answered Duke Huan of Qi preserved was only a few.

literal: Yet the deed of greatest virtue must await great peace; if it is not the right man, it only invites spiritual punishment.
idiomatic: Yet the deed of greatest virtue must await great peace; if it is not the right man, it only invites spiritual punishment.

literal: Qin Huang was without the Way and brought the disaster of rain and wind;
idiomatic: Qin Huang was without the Way and brought the disaster of rain and wind;

literal: Han Wu was extravagant and licentious and suffered the harm of the carriage that bore his coffin.
idiomatic: Han Wu was extravagant and licentious and suffered the harm of the carriage that bore his coffin.

literal: When Emperor Wendi received the Mandate the flame of Han shone anew; the four seas flowed in peace and the realm was united. Swords were bestowed on knights and horses yoked to the drum carriage—only then did he use Zhang Chun's text and begin to follow Boyang's teaching.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wendi received the Mandate the flame of Han shone anew; the four seas flowed in peace and the realm was united. Swords were bestowed on knights and horses yoked to the drum carriage—only then did he use Zhang Chun's text and begin to follow Boyang's teaching.

literal: As for Wei and Jin, though each had its ruler, they measured virtue and took their place and none could be compared in deliberation.
idiomatic: As for Wei and Jin, though each had its ruler, they measured virtue and took their place, and none could be compared in such deliberation.

literal: Jiang Ji memorialized before and only soiled paper and ink;
idiomatic: Jiang Ji's memorial came before and only soiled paper and ink;

literal: Yuan Zhun issued his treatise after and in the end it was not carried out.
idiomatic: Yuan Zhun's treatise came after and in the end was not carried out.

literal: The age has passed through three courts and the years approach ten reign-periods; the season of opening sagehood is now this splendid assembly.
idiomatic: The age has passed through three courts and the years approach ten reign-periods; the season of opening sagehood is now this splendid assembly.

literal: Yet since the power of water ceased to contend, the passes of Hangu were sealed; the heavenly horse ceased its song and the tribute of thatched bundles was cut off.
idiomatic: Yet since the power of water ceased to contend, the passes of Hangu were sealed; the heavenly horse ceased its song and the tribute of thatched bundles was cut off.

literal: Our Grand Ancestor gathered the omen of the treasure cock and grasped the book of the phoenix, with one virtue to set the court aright and bowing to three parts to serve his lord, scattering these demon bands as easily as pouring boiling water on snow.
idiomatic: Our Grand Ancestor gathered the omen of the treasure cock and grasped the book of the phoenix, with one virtue to set the court aright and bowing to three parts to serve his lord, scattering these demon bands as easily as pouring boiling water on snow.

literal: But when Chang received the Mandate, Fa then carried out punishment; though the Great White rose high and the Central Land ought to fight, he set it outside his measure and looked for them to turn to goodness.
idiomatic: But when Chang received the Mandate, Fa then carried out punishment; though the Great White rose high and the Central Land ought to fight, he set it outside his measure and looked for them to turn to goodness.

literal: I bow before Your Majesty's divine martial bearing and heaven-given strategy—horses many as in Jibei, generals unlike those of Shanxi; when the cool wind comes and white dew falls, you will march north to the Taihang and east to Jieshi, about to swallow Ba-Shu and sweep Xiao-Han, to park Long Isle and pool the Jiang-Han.
idiomatic: I bow before Your Majesty's divine martial bearing and heaven-given strategy—horses many as in Jibei, generals unlike those of Shanxi; when the cool wind comes and white dew falls, you will march north to the Taihang and east to Jieshi, about to swallow Ba-Shu and sweep Xiao-Han, to park Long Isle and pool the Jiang-Han.

literal: Yet I fear that if we meet the wind and set the fire, wormwood and mugwort will burn together; if we press these six armies, the nine punishments will not be declared.
idiomatic: Yet I fear that if we meet the wind and set the fire, wormwood and mugwort will burn together; if we press these six armies, the nine punishments will not be declared.

literal: When Zhou Fa sent the jade tally and Han dispatched the bamboo envoy, the meaning lay in succoring the people, not in love of war.
idiomatic: When Zhou Fa sent the jade tally and Han dispatched the bamboo envoy, the meaning lay in succoring the people, not in love of war.

literal: As for the saying about casting at a rat and fearing the vessel, that is common talk;
idiomatic: As for the saying about casting at a rat and fearing the vessel, that is common talk;

literal: the words about civil virtue embracing the distant do not know expedient policy.
idiomatic: the words about civil virtue embracing the distant do not know expedient policy.

literal: Now the sons of the Three Terraces and the good families of the six commanderies store their edge and wait for the hour, wrap their grain and await the edict.
idiomatic: Now the sons of the Three Terraces and the good families of the six commanderies store their edge and wait for the hour, wrap their grain and await the edict.

literal: Better to drive the dragon carriage in tiger garb, first gather the people of Longyou, turn like lightning and startle like thunder, and then take the lands of southern Jing.
idiomatic: Better to drive the dragon carriage in tiger garb, first gather the people of Longyou, turn like lightning and startle like thunder, and then take the lands of southern Jing.

literal: In old times Qin raised Changping and the metal essence devoured Mao; Chu attacked Julu and the crooked arrow streamed across the sky—how much more, with our majesty and spirit, can there be no concerted aid?
idiomatic: In old times Qin raised Changping and the metal essence devoured Mao; Chu attacked Julu and the crooked arrow streamed across the sky—how much more, with our majesty and spirit, can there be no concerted aid?

literal: Only let their common people once behold the six armies—they will seem to see the King of Zhou, or to meet the Minister of Correction.
idiomatic: Only let their common people once behold the six armies—they will seem to see the King of Zhou, or to meet the Minister of Correction.

literal: Then remove their harsh orders and give them your compact laws, shake the ranks and return, halt the weapons and make martial virtue a name only, plant the golden marker on the southern sea and carve stone on the eastern mountain, recording heaven and earth's strange achievement and spreading your wind-sound for a thousand years.
idiomatic: Then remove their harsh orders and give them your compact laws, shake the ranks and return, halt the weapons and make martial virtue a name only, plant the golden marker on the southern sea and carve stone on the eastern mountain, recording heaven and earth's strange achievement and spreading your renown for a thousand years.

literal: If Ma Huang were not dead and Ziyang still stood, you would then consult the diagram of the Bright Hall and draft the rite of shooting the ox, comparing virtue and discussing merit—you would be shamed beside the men of old. To ascend the central peak and announce fengshan—your servant has doubts.
idiomatic: If Ma Huang were not dead and Ziyang still stood, you would then consult the diagram of the Bright Hall and draft the rite of shooting the ox, comparing virtue and discussing merit—you would be shamed beside the men of old. To ascend the central peak and announce fengshan—your servant has doubts.

literal: He was again questioned on seeking talent and examining office; Xun answered:
idiomatic: He was again questioned on seeking talent and examining office; Xun answered:

literal: Your servant has heard that carved beasts and painted dragons have only the air of wind and clouds;
idiomatic: Your servant has heard that carved beasts and painted dragons have only the air of wind and clouds;

literal: golden boats and jade horses in the end have no achievement on water or land.
idiomatic: golden boats and jade horses in the end have no achievement on water or land.

literal: Three times to drive the carriage and honor the worthy is to gather what is truly useful; one hair not plucked—what is there to take?
idiomatic: Three times to drive the carriage and honor the worthy is to gather what is truly useful; one hair not plucked—what is there to take?

literal: Therefore Yao made Yu guest and thereby preserved the conduct of Mount Ji;
idiomatic: Therefore Yao made Yu guest and thereby preserved the conduct of Mount Ji;

literal: Zhou moved the tripod of Shang and did not admit the words of the lone bamboo.
idiomatic: Zhou moved the tripod of Shang and did not admit the words of the lone bamboo.

literal: Yet recluses who steal a name have long been so;
idiomatic: Yet recluses who steal a name have long been so;

literal: court ministers who usurp place are also truly many.
idiomatic: court ministers who usurp place are also truly many.

literal: When Han invested the chief minister, there was at once the omen of bells and drums;
idiomatic: When Han invested the chief minister, there was at once the omen of bells and drums;

literal: when Wei used the Three Dukes, it brought Sun Quan's laughter.
idiomatic: when Wei used the Three Dukes, it brought Sun Quan's laughter.

literal: Thus mountain forest and court can each tolerate blame and praise;
idiomatic: Thus mountain forest and court can each tolerate blame and praise;

literal: fat reclusion and honored guest in turn have their better and worse.
idiomatic: fat reclusion and honored guest in turn have their better and worse.

literal: As for times that were not crossing the sea yet saying it shames one to be a subject of Qin;
idiomatic: As for times that were not crossing the sea yet saying it shames one to be a subject of Qin;

literal: affairs unlike leaving the passes yet speaking of shame at following Wei's disorder.
idiomatic: affairs unlike leaving the passes yet speaking of shame at following Wei's disorder.

literal: Though the stars trespass on the Emperor's seat, they do not alter a heart set on loftiness;
idiomatic: Though the stars trespass on the Emperor's seat, they do not alter a heart set on loftiness;

literal: though the moon offends the Lesser Apex, they still keep a straight and unyielding will.
idiomatic: though the moon offends the Lesser Apex, they still keep a straight and unyielding will.

literal: Since our Grand Ancestor, we have broadened the great enterprise—from Yu reaching the Divine Ancestor, from Shun matching the Literary Ancestor.
idiomatic: Since our Grand Ancestor, we have broadened the great enterprise—from Yu reaching the Divine Ancestor, from Shun matching the Literary Ancestor.

literal: Your Majesty received heaven's bright mandate, your glory eclipsing sun and moon; from accepting the regency you matched the Literary Ancestor, taking heaven and earth as model to set offices and stars as image to spread duties.
idiomatic: Your Majesty received heaven's bright mandate, your glory eclipsing sun and moon; from accepting the regency you matched the Literary Ancestor, taking heaven and earth as model to set offices and stars as image to spread duties.

literal: Han of the Divine Phoenix was shamed to use it only for chronology;
idiomatic: Han of the Divine Phoenix was shamed to use it only for chronology;

literal: Wei of the Blue Dragon was ashamed to change the reign title.
idiomatic: Wei of the Blue Dragon was ashamed to change the reign title.

literal: Above you answer to the arrayed stars—all are uncommon men;
idiomatic: Above you answer to the arrayed stars—all are uncommon men;

literal: below you take mountains and rivers as law—none are not strange knights.
idiomatic: below you take mountains and rivers as law—none are not strange knights.

literal: Therefore in the painted hall and armored watchtower virtue is renewed day by day; in the temple cauldrons and singing bells royal merit is entrusted year by year.
idiomatic: Therefore in the painted hall and armored watchtower virtue is renewed day by day; in the temple cauldrons and singing bells royal merit is entrusted year by year.
